# Command line

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-cli-docs.ts from the command definitions. Do not edit by hand; run `bun run docs:cli`. -->

`conveyor <command> [options]`. Every command takes the global options, `--help` prints a command's
options, and `--json` prints machine-readable output where a command has any. Nothing reads a
plaintext credential from a command argument: passwords come from a prompt without echo, a file, or
stdin (`-`).

The home is `--home`, else `CONVEYOR_HOME`, else `~/.conveyor`; the `service` commands, `upgrade` and
`rollback` default to the home recorded in the installed systemd unit, so they also work under
`sudo`. The configuration is `--config`, else `<home>/config/conveyor.yaml`.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| ---: | --- |
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | The command ran and failed (an operation error, a failed check, a timeout) |
| 2 | The command line is invalid |
| 3 | The configuration does not load or validate |
| 4 | The running service cannot be reached (it is stopped, or there is no control socket) |
| 5 | The service refused the request because a precondition does not hold (the reason is printed) |

## Global options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--home <dir>` | Conveyor home (default: $CONVEYOR_HOME, else ~/.conveyor) |
| `--config <file>` | configuration entrypoint (default: &lt;home>/config/conveyor.yaml) |
| `--json` | print machine-readable JSON |
| `--help` | show help for the command |

## Commands

### `conveyor init`

Create the Conveyor home, a starter configuration and the first administrator.

Safe to repeat: existing files are kept, a configuration cloned into &lt;home>/config is used as is, and the administrator is created only while no dashboard account exists.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--admin-username <name>` | the first administrator's username (prompted on a terminal) |
| `--admin-password-file <file\|->` | read the administrator's password from a file (- for stdin) |

### `conveyor doctor`

Check the home, configuration and every external prerequisite, with fixes.

### `conveyor version`

Print the version and build metadata.

### `conveyor config check`

Validate the configuration and print each repository's compiled plan.

### `conveyor config show`

Print the effective configuration, with !secret values redacted.

### `conveyor config compare [<left>] <right>`

Compile two configurations and compare their plans (left defaults to the current configuration).

### `conveyor config migrate`

Write a tag-based conveyor.yaml reproducing a configuration directory, and verify it.

Instruction files are copied into the new directory; script, folder and state paths are kept as they are, so the compiled plans stay identical. Exits 1 when the result is not identical.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--from <dir-or-file>` | the configuration to migrate (default: --config) |
| `--to <dir>` | an absent or empty directory for the new configuration |

### `conveyor config builtin [<file>]`

List the packaged defaults, or print one to copy and adapt.

### `conveyor serve`

Run Conveyor in the foreground (the service unit runs this).

CONVEYOR_USERNAME with CONVEYOR_PASSWORD_HASH still seed the first administrator when no account exists (compatibility); `conveyor init` is the supported way.

### `conveyor service install`

Install the systemd system unit that runs conveyor serve under a non-root account (sudo).

Records the home, configuration and executable in the unit; enables but does not start it. The home and the install prefix must belong to the account, so it can run, upgrade and roll back without root.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--account <user>` | the account the service runs as (default: the user who ran sudo) |
| `--path <PATH>` | PATH for the service: where git, gh, bwrap and the agent CLIs are |
| `--unit <name>` | the systemd unit name (default: conveyor) |

### `conveyor service start`

Start the service and wait until it answers (sudo).

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--unit <name>` | the systemd unit name (default: conveyor) |

### `conveyor service stop`

Stop the service, optionally draining running work first (sudo).

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--unit <name>` | the systemd unit name (default: conveyor) |
| `--drain` | stop admitting work and wait for running work to finish first |
| `--timeout <duration>` | how long --drain waits (default 30m); then it gives up and admits work again |
| `--force` | with --drain: go ahead when the timeout passes (running work is interrupted and resumes after the next start) |

### `conveyor service restart`

Restart the service; with --drain it waits for running work and needs no sudo.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--unit <name>` | the systemd unit name (default: conveyor) |
| `--drain` | stop admitting work and wait for running work to finish first |
| `--timeout <duration>` | how long --drain waits (default 30m); then it gives up and admits work again |
| `--force` | with --drain: go ahead when the timeout passes (running work is interrupted and resumes after the next start) |

### `conveyor service status`

Show the unit's state and the running service.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--unit <name>` | the systemd unit name (default: conveyor) |

### `conveyor service uninstall`

Stop, disable and remove the unit; the home and installed releases are kept (sudo).

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--unit <name>` | the systemd unit name (default: conveyor) |

### `conveyor status`

Show versions, paths, dashboard URL, service health, capacity, stopped items and disk usage.

### `conveyor board`

List the items Conveyor tracks with their stage and state.

### `conveyor item show <item>`

Explain an item's stage, its concrete blocker and the recovery actions available.

### `conveyor item history <item>`

List an item's stage transitions, oldest first.

### `conveyor item logs <item>`

Print an item's run history (agent events, tool calls, checks), optionally following it.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--follow` | keep printing new events until interrupted |

### `conveyor item retry <item>`

Retry a blocked, errored or needs-intervention item at its current stage.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--note <text>` | a note added to the item's conversation |

### `conveyor item pause <item>`

Pause an item (removes its enrollment label; its stage and worktree are kept).

### `conveyor item resume <item>`

Resume a paused item.

### `conveyor questions list`

List the open questions agents asked.

### `conveyor questions answer <question-id> <answer...>`

Answer an open question; the item continues where it stopped.

### `conveyor logs`

Print the service log (it does not need the service running), optionally following it.

Agent transcripts are not in the service log: use conveyor item logs &lt;item>.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--follow` | keep printing new records until interrupted |
| `--level <level>` | minimum level: debug, info, warn or error |
| `--since <duration>` | only records from this long ago, e.g. 30m, 1h, 7d |
| `--item <item>` | only records about this item, e.g. conveyor:90 |
| `--stage <stage>` | only records about this stage |
| `--lines <n>` | print at most the last n matching records (default 200; 0 for all) |

### `conveyor upgrade`

Download, verify and switch to another release, draining running work first.

Steps: verify the archive's checksum, install it beside the current release, validate the configuration with it, then (service running) stop admitting work, wait for running work, back up the database, switch and restart, and wait until the new release reports ready. Configuration and data are never changed by an upgrade apart from the new release's database migrations.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--version <vX.Y.Z>` | the release to install (default: the latest) |
| `--archive <file>` | install this release archive instead of downloading it (needs --checksums) |
| `--checksums <file>` | the release's checksums.txt, for --archive |
| `--prefix <dir>` | the install prefix (default: the one this conveyor runs from) |
| `--drain-timeout <duration>` | how long running work may take to finish before the switch is cancelled (default 30m) |
| `--wait-timeout <duration>` | how long to wait for the new release to report ready after the drain (default 5m) |
| `--no-wait` | return once the service accepted the switch (for a deploy stage upgrading Conveyor itself) |

### `conveyor rollback`

Return to the release the last upgrade replaced.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--restore-backup` | also restore the database saved before that upgrade (required when the upgrade migrated it; later work is lost) |
| `--prefix <dir>` | the install prefix (default: the one this conveyor runs from) |
| `--drain-timeout <duration>` | how long running work may take to finish before the switch is cancelled (default 30m) |
| `--wait-timeout <duration>` | how long to wait for the new release to report ready after the drain (default 5m) |
| `--no-wait` | return once the service accepted the switch (for a deploy stage upgrading Conveyor itself) |

### `conveyor cleanup`

Prune finished work past the retention policy (run events and per-run artifacts).

Only runs of items that are closed, done or offboarded (and finished steering runs) are pruned; open items keep everything they may need to resume. Service logs rotate by settings.logging.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | report what would be deleted without deleting it |
| `--run-history <duration>` | this time instead of settings.retention.runHistory |
| `--artifacts <duration>` | this time instead of settings.retention.artifacts |

### `conveyor diagnostics export`

Write a redacted diagnostics bundle for a bug report, with a manifest of what it holds.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--output <file.tar.gz>` | where to write it (default: ./conveyor-diagnostics-&lt;time>.tar.gz) |

### `conveyor admin reset-password <username>`

Set a dashboard account's password and sign out its sessions.

Works whether or not the service is running: it uses the same account store the dashboard does.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--password-file <file\|->` | read the new password from a file (- for stdin) instead of prompting |
